10047539:
An Act to Create a Fund to Spread Awareness of Maine's Working Waterfronts
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development April 9, 2025
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development:
My name is Jessica Joyce, and I own small business in Freeport, Tidal Bay Consulting. I have spent over 20 years working in public policy focused on fisheries policy, coastal community climate adaptation, and working waterfront. I am writing to support LD 1245.
Over the past several years, I worked on several grants and contracts providing direct technical assistance to, and resources for, public and private owners of working waterfront. Due to changes in sea levels, shifts in fisheries distribution, and an evolving marine economy, there is a need for technical assistance to municipalities and wharf owners, who are often limited in capacity to fundraise for, and manage these projects. These projects range from general infrastructure maintenance and rebuilding after storms, to comprehensive planning, inventorying and permitting. Having a standing fund for towns and regional planning organizations to support technical assistance for these initiatives is a priority to preserve working waterfront, along with funding for the implementation of these projects.
In addition, having access to funding to create informational materials to provide education and outreach materials and/or plan events to help inform Maine's residents and tourists about the importance of preserving (and coexisting with) the working waterfront. The Maine Coast Fishermen's Association has partnered with several organizations and municipalities to create a brochure, referred to as the "Scuttlebutt", to educate residents on how to live in a working waterfront town. Every coastal town could benefit from a similar public awareness campaign to support our blue economy.
If enacted and implemented, LD 1245 will serve a critical need for the fishing and aquaculture industries in Maine and our marine economy, both to help community members understand working waterfront and to provide low or no-cost technical assistance to municipalities.
Thank you for consideration of this testimony.
Jessica Gribbon Joyce

Testimony of Joe Oliva, Outreach and Communications Director of GrowSmart Maine
in support of LD 1245, An Act to Create a Fund to Spread Awareness of Maine's Working Waterfronts
April 25, 2025
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and Honorable Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development,
My name is Joe Oliva and I am the Outreach and Communications Director for GrowSmart Maine. We are a statewide non-partisan non-profit organization helping communities navigate change in alignment with smart growth. We advocate for comprehensive policies and funding for smart growth practices and outcomes.
The fund established by LD 1245 is not just a step in the right direction - it is a necessary tool in the effort to support and protect working waterfronts in Maine. Working waterfront properties are the keystones of our coastal communities as economic drivers and conservators of cherished ways of life. Yet, mounting pressures related to growth, gentrification, climate change, and other factors have precipitated what amounts to an existential threat for many of these already limited resources.
GrowSmart Maine supports passage of LD 1245 as it relates to a core tenet of our organization: "it's better to change than to be changed". The resources provided through the fund will be used for information campaigns aimed at raising awareness of the aforementioned issues and help strengthen a coalition of advocates and stakeholders who understand the gravity of what's at play for many of Maine's coastal communities. Technical assistance funds provided through this program will further buoy the efforts of stakeholders and community members to navigate rapid macro-level change in ways that make sense at the local level.
The Working Waterfront Information and Technical Assistance Fund is a much needed tool for the state as we, collectively, balance addressing the needs of current and future residents as they relate to housing, transportation, and other growth-related challenges while preserving access to local natural resources, heritage industries, and the invaluable sense of place felt in every Maine community.

Good afternoon Senator Curry, Representative Gere and distinguished members of the Joint
Standing Coimnittee on Housing and Economic Development. My name is Morgan Rielly, andI represent House District 127, which includes part of Westbrook. I am here today to present LD 1245, "An Act to Create a Fund to Spread Awareness of Maine's Working Waterfronts."
LD 1245 will establish a non-lapsing fund within the Maine Office of Community Affairs
(MOCA) to receive state, federal or private monies to spread awareness of Maine's working
waterfronts. After speaking with Director Horn, she suggested broadening the fund's scope to
allow MOCA to include technical assistance for communities to encourage the protection and
development of working waterfronts. I think this is a great idea and have attached an amendment
to my testimony with the changes.
The idea for this bill first came to me while working out on oyster farms in Casco Bay during
conversations with sea farmers, shellfish harvesters, commercial fishermen and advocates for our working waterfronts. Our state is currently down to 20 miles of working waterfront out of a
coastline of 5,000 miles. While we have been losing our working waterfronts to gentrification for decades, we've seen an acceleration over the past five years due to many people from
out-of-state moving to our coastal and island communities. While a growing population is a good thing for our state's economy, it also presents issues with a lack of knowledge of the historic
importance of our marine-based industries and the need to protect access to our waterfronts. We
have also witnessed the destruction of our Working waterfronts to increasingly powerful storms,
like the ones that destroyed many working waterfront properties last year.

Testimony of the Maine Office of Community Affairs Director Samantha Horn May 2, 2025
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Housing and Economic Development In Support of LD 1245 An Act to Create a Fund to
Spread Awareness of Maine's Working Waterfronts
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and Members of the joint standing committee on Housing and Economic Development, my name is Samantha Horn, Director of the Maine Office of Community Affairs. I am submitting written testimony in support of LD 1245, An Act to Create a Fund to Spread Awareness of Maine's Working Waterfronts. My testimony in support of the bill is based on the sponsor's amendment.
The Maine Office of Community Affairs, or MOCA, was created in 2024 to foster communication and partnerships between the State and communities in this State. Our charge is to engage with municipalities, tribal governments and regional councils to provide coordinated and efficient planning, technical assistance and financial support to better plan for challenges, pursue solutions and create stronger, more resilient communities.
Working waterfronts are a precious and limited resource that keeps Maine's economy and culture strong. Maine Won't Wait and the Governor's Infrastructure Rebuilding and Resilience Commission have highlighted the vulnerability of our working waterfronts and challenged us to protect and strengthen them.
The Maine Coastal Program is proposed in the biennial budget to be transferred to MOCA. The Coastal Program has a strong presence in the working waterfront discussion and MOCA as a whole organization will have substantial expertise in community planning and resilience. Especially in these times of federal funding uncertainty, it makes sense to have a non-lapsing fund that can accept grants and donations to provide communications and technical assistance services in support of working waterfronts, and for MOCA to be the place to house such a fund.
Uses of the fund could be as varied as brochures or advertisements highlighting the importance of working waterfronts; contracts with service providers to assist towns to design public forums, plans, ordinances and information campaigns about working waterfronts; or facilitation for groups that are trying to come to regional or local agreement on strategies for protecting working waterfront properties and facilities.
For those reasons, the Administration supports LD 1245 with the proposed amendment. Thank you for your time. I am happy to provide information for the work session.
192317:
May 2025
RE: LD 1245 - An Act to Create a Fund to Spread Awareness of Maine's Working Waterfronts
Senator Curry, Representative Gere, and members of the Committee on Housing and Economic
Development,
My name is Stacey Keefer. I am a resident of Union and l am testifying today in my capacity as
Director for the Maine Marine Trades Association (MMTA). MMTA represents over 120 Maine
businesses and an industry comprised of boatyards, boat builders, marinas, boat dealers,
marine retailers, and many businesses who are part of, or who serve, working waterfronts.
MMTA would like to thank Representative Reilly and co-sponsors of LD 1245 for acknowledging
the needs of working waterfronts, especially recognizing a lack of education for tourists and
new coastal residents regarding working waterfront value and vulnerability. Awareness and
education campaigns could help build stronger communities where working waterfront businesses are embraced for their historic significance, economic contributions, and lifestyle diversity along a coast that is becoming alarmingly gentrified. Tourists already enjoy fresh Maine seafood but often miss the connection between their tasty lunch and the need for
working waterfront preservation. New residents need to understand that working waterfronts may create a little noise and look a little different, but their operations cannot exist elsewhere
and are essential to our Maine's economy and food supply.
MMTA has taken on an example of our own education campaign with the help of a NOAA
Marine Debris Coalition Grant. Our education campaign is aimed at marine debris prevention
with an emphasis on teaching recreational boaters how to best navigate around fishing and sea
farming gear in order to prevent marine debris and economic harm to our businesses in the
fishing industry. To my knowledge, the State has never provided this type of information to our visiting boaters or new boaters, so we are pleased to be collaborating to fulfil that need.
Just this week the Working Waterfront Coalition was discussing a need for help with
communications. MMTA appreciates that the proposed fund in LD 1245 could be supported by
both private and public sources but managed strategically and more effectively by the State.
Thank you for your consideration and we urge you to support LD 1245. I am happy to answer
questions.
Respectfully,
Stacey Keefer
Maine Marine Trades Association, Executive Director

Senator Curry, Representative Gere, Honorable members of the Joint Committee on Housing and Economic Development:
My name is Sebastian Belle and I am the Executive Director of the Maine Aquaculture Association (MAA). The MAA is the oldest state aquaculture association in the country. We are a volunteer membership association whose board of directors is selected to represent the diversity of the aquaculture sector in terms of species, production method and company size. Irrespective of company size each company has one vote. We represent Maine's aquatic farmers that raise finfish, shellfish and sea vegetables. Our farmers annually produce over 100 million dollars in farm gate revenue and directly employ roughly 700 Maine citizens year-round. We purchase goods and services from over 400 Maine businesses and our total economic impact is roughly 150 million dollars annually.
I stand before you today to testify in strong support of LD 1245 "An Act to Create a Fund to Spread Awareness of Maine's Working Waterfronts". The MAA is one of the Founding Members of the Maine Working Waterfront Coalition. Our members live and work up and down Maine's coastline and rely on working waterfront properties to conduct our businesses. Sadly, Maine's working waterfronts are in danger of being overwhelmed by gentrification and conversion to residential uses. Although working waterfronts are part of the iconic Maine brand many new residents know very little about them. Efforts to educate the public about working waterfronts have been haphazard and woefully under funded. LD 1245 seeks to bring existing state resources to bear on this important issue and begin to help the public understand what working waterfronts are and why they are so important to our coastal communities.
I ask that you to vote Ought To Pass on LD 1245 and help support a big part of Maine's iconic brand. Thank you for your attention, I would be glad to answer any questions you may have.
Sincerely,
